title: the system device publishes the host's name, and claude_identity asks it there
intention: claude_identity.who() names this box's host on every OS Cairn runs on, Windows included. It asks the system device through a tool that device publishes, cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/host, so saveslate stops crashing on Windows and no tool reaches unpublished device code.
why: Akien, 2026-11-21, relayed verbatim by akiendelllinux_cc_orchestrator: "hostname should come from the system device." Measured: saveslate crashed on akiendell (Windows) at cairn/tools/base/claude_identity.py:108, '"host": os.uname().nodename', because os.uname does not exist on Windows. Saveslate auto-commit 4794006a7 (2026-11-20 19:54) changed the line to call cairn.devices.system_rackmount.rackmount.host_name, which was the right home but the wrong path. system_rackmount's public_interface is [], so the import is a RULE 1 breach, and encapsulation_breaches reds it on main today. That commit carried no ticket and no proof.
traces_to: RULE 1 (a device's public interface is the bus plus any client tool it publishes); Law 8 (4794006a7 entered proven-space with no proof); Law 3 (the Windows crash is measured at n=1, from a packet still unread).
how: Move host_name() and os_id() out of cairn/devices/system_rackmount/rackmount.py into a new published tool, cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/host/host.py. The spelling stays platform.node().split('.')[0].lower() and platform.system().lower(), with no socket import. The tool gets a charter shaped like cairn/devices/trouble/tools/store/intention+why.json: published_by_device true, and public_interface naming exactly cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host. It is written through the artifact door before BUILDME. rackmount.py keeps neither function, because nothing else calls them. claude_identity.who() imports host_name lazily from the published module. The system_rackmount charter's public_interface names the module. Two red-first proofs: one in tools/base for who() and its imports (clauses 1-2), and one beside the tool for the tool alone (clause 3).

clauses.claim: with os.uname deleted from the os module for the length of the call, claude_identity.who() returns a dict whose host is non-empty, contains no '.', equals its own lowercase, and equals cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host.host_name()

build_inspector.encapsulation_breaches lists no row whose file is cairn/tools/base/claude_identity.py, and claude_identity.py imports cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host and no other cairn.devices module

the published tool alone: with os.uname deleted, host_name() is non-empty, has no '.', and is lowercase; os_id() is one of windows, linux, darwin; host.py imports no socket; and its intention+why.json declares published_by_device true with public_interface exactly ['cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host']

decisions.text: D1: the published tool. cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/host/host.py holds host_name() and os_id() moved from rackmount.py, with their docstrings ('the one place the os calls live'). Its intention+why.json follows the trouble/tools/store shape: published_by_device true, public_interface [the one module], owner none of its own (a tool has users), and held by system_rackmount.
D2: rackmount.py keeps neither function. Measured 2026-11-21: nothing but claude_identity calls rackmount.host_name or rackmount.os_id.
D3: claude_identity.who() imports host_name from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host, lazily inside who() as it does today.
D4: the system_rackmount charter's public_interface names cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host. The write rides the artifact door.

D5: a red-first proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_who_names_the_host_through_the_system_device.py, PROVES {1, 2}. Tooth 1 deletes os.uname (getattr/delattr, restored in finally) and calls who() over a scratch sessions dir. Tooth 2 reads encapsulation_breaches('.') for rows from claude_identity.py and the module's ImportFrom targets by ast.
D6: a red-first proof cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/host/proofs/test_the_host_tool_names_the_box.py, PROVES {3}, measuring the tool alone.

out: validation_store.host_name and every other host-name site (spanning ticket B, one door names the host)
a bus verb for the host's name (the no-bus callers rule it out)
